scenario.name: Microsoft Security Auditing & CISA DFIR — Active Directory DCSync DRSUAPI Replication (EventID 4662)
scenario.overview: Imagine a royal mint where sister vaults regularly synchronize their master gold ledgers over a private courier channel. Wearing a compromised supervisor badge from an ordinary office workstation, an intruder calls the royal mint pretending to be a sister vault, clears the special ledger-sync checkpoint, and receives a freshly packaged copy of every master household seal without ever setting foot inside the vault room. In this scenario (T1003.006, Microsoft Security Auditing & CISA DFIR, Active Directory DCSync DRSUAPI Replication , EventID 4662), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: mS-DRSR RPC Bind to UUID, then directory Replication Extended Rights Check, then replication of SupplementalCredentials. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering MS-DRSR RPC Bind to UUID, then Directory Replication Extended Rights Check, then Replication of SupplementalCredentials, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on SIEM Event 4624 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: MS-DRSR RPC Bind to UUID e3514235-4b06-11d1-ab04-00c04fc2dcd2 (EventID 4624 & Zeek dce_rpc)
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1003.006 - OS Credential Dumping: DCSync)
stages.description: Dialing straight from a regular employee desk rather than a registered sister vault, the intruder rings the royal mint exclusive directory-sync extension using a hijacked high-clearance pass. From a compromised workstation (10.10.4.22), the attacker authenticates over SMB/RPC (Security EventID 4624 LogonType 3) to CORP-DC01 and binds to the Directory Replication Service (drsuapi) RPC interface UUID e3514235-4b06-11d1-ab04-00c04fc2dcd2 via IDL_DRSBind (logged in Network Event 4624 with Protocol=MS-DRSR / DRSUAPI over TCP High Port, RpcInterfaceUuid=e3514235-4b06-11d1-ab04-00c04fc2dcd2, SourceWorkstationIp=10.10.4.22 , Non-DC IP, TargetDomainController=CORP-DC01 , 10.10.0.10 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes lsadump::dcsync /domain:corp.local /user:corp\krbtgt (which Binds to the Domain Controller's MS-DRSR Directory Replication Service RPC interface , UUID e3514235-4b06-11d1-ab04-00c04fc2dcd2 and invokes IDL_DR so that impersonates a Domain Controller over the network , T1003.006 during "MS-DRSR RPC Bind to UUID e3514235-4b06-11d1-ab04-00c04fc2dcd2 , EventID 4624 & Zeek dce_rpc" to replicate NTLM hashes, AES-256 keys, and password history for krbtgt and Domain Admins without touching lsass.exe or ntds.dit on disk). Next, the follow-up artifact impacket-secretsdump corp.local/svc_sync@10.10.0.10 -just-dc-user krbtgt runs (which Constructs or requests Kerberos AS-REQ , EventID 4768 or TGS-REQ , EventID 4769 tickets against the Key Distribution Center , KDC, specifying custo so that compromises Active Directory authentication and service ticket cryptography , T1003.006 during "MS-DRSR RPC Bind to UUID e3514235-4b06-11d1-ab04-00c04fc2dcd2 , EventID 4624 & Zeek dce_rpc" to escalate domain privileges or crack service account credentials offline). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ DCE-RPC Bind UUID e3514235-4b06-11d1-ab04-00c04fc2dcd2 (drsuapi) from 10.10.4.22 / ⇠#1 RESP 4624) from Node ① (#1 Rogue Workstation (10.10.4.22)) to Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AD Naming Context (DC=corp)).

stages.title: Stage 2: Directory Replication Extended Rights Check (Security EventID 4662 ControlAccess 0x100)
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1003.006 - EventID 4662 Extended Rights GUIDs)
stages.description: When the caller asks to download the secret password ledger, the royal mint security clerk checks two distinct special permission stamps on the caller badge (one permitting directory changes and a second permitting secret fields) and writes an unforgeable receipt in the vault access book. When IDL_DRSGetNCChanges (Opnum 3) is invoked, CORP-DC01 logs Windows Security EventID 4662 (An operation was performed on an object) on ObjectType domainDNS (%{19195a5b-6da0-11d0-afd3-00c04fd930c9}) with AccessMask 0x100 (ControlAccess) and Properties containing the Extended Rights GUIDs 1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2 (DS-Replication-Get-Changes) and 1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2 (DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All) (logged in WinEvent Event 4662 with EventID=4662 , Directory Service Object Access, SubjectUserName=svc_sync , Non-DC Account, AccessMask=0x100 , ControlAccess, ExtendedRightGuid=1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2 , DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes EventID 4662: AccessMask=0x100 (ControlAccess) ObjectServer=DS (which Binds to the Domain Controller's MS-DRSR Directory Replication Service RPC interface , UUID e3514235-4b06-11d1-ab04-00c04fc2dcd2 and invokes IDL_DR so that impersonates a Domain Controller over the network , T1003.006 during "Directory Replication Extended Rights Check , Security EventID 4662 ControlAccess 0x100" to replicate NTLM hashes, AES-256 keys, and password history for krbtgt and Domain Admins without touching lsass.exe or ntds.dit on disk). Next, the follow-up artifact DS-Replication-Get-Changes: {1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2} runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , DS-Replication-Get-Changes: {1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2} via System / Runtime Exec so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.006 during "Directory Replication Extended Rights Check , Security EventID 4662 ControlAccess 0x100" , When IDL_DRSGetNCChanges , Opnum 3 is invoked, CORP-DC01 logs Windows Security EventID 4662 , An operation was performed on an object on ObjectType domainDNS , %{19195a5b-6da0-11d0-afd3-00c04fd930c9} with AccessMask 0x100 , ControlAccess and Properties containing the Extended Rights GUIDs 1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2 , DS-Replication-Get-Changes and 1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2 , DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ IDL_DRSGetNCChanges DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All {1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2} / ⇠#2 ACK 4662) from Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch) to Node ③ (#3 DC RPC Endpoint Mapper (:135)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AD Naming Context (DC=corp)).

stages.title: Stage 3: Replication of SupplementalCredentials & krbtgt AES-256 / NTLM Hashes
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1003.006 - krbtgt Key Material Exfiltration)
stages.description: Satisfied by the permission stamps, the royal mint seals up the master kingdom stamp and every citizen secret seal inside an encrypted courier pouch and ships them straight back to the intruder desk. CORP-DC01 returns the DRS_MSG_GETNCCHANGESREPLY structure encrypted with the RPC session key, delivering the current and historical NTLM hashes, AES-256 Kerberos keys, and SupplementalCredentials for krbtgt to the attacker workstation for Golden Ticket forgery (logged in Network Event 3 with RpcOperation=IDL_DRSGetNCChanges , Opnum 3, ReplicatedObject=CN=krbtgt,CN=Users,DC=corp,DC=local, ReplicatedAttributes=unicodePwd, supplementalCredentials , AES256/NTLM, IncidentResponseAction=Double krbtgt password reset required so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes RPC Reply: DRS_MSG_GETNCCHANGESREPLY (Attributes: unicodePwd, dBCSPwd, supplementalCredentials) (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , RPC Reply: DRS_MSG_GETNCCHANGESREPLY , Attributes: unicodePwd, dBCSPwd, supplementalCredenti so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.006 during "Replication of SupplementalCredentials & krbtgt AES-256 / NTLM Hashes" , CORP-DC01 returns the DRS_MSG_GETNCCHANGESREPLY structure encrypted with the RPC session key, delivering the current and historical NTLM hashes, AES-256 Kerberos keys, and SupplementalCredentials for krbtgt to the attacker workstation for Golden Ticket forgery while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Extracted Hash: krbtgt:502:aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:88e4d91a03b7190441a9c12098765432::: runs (which Constructs or requests Kerberos AS-REQ , EventID 4768 or TGS-REQ , EventID 4769 tickets against the Key Distribution Center , KDC, specifying custo so that compromises Active Directory authentication and service ticket cryptography , T1003.006 during "Replication of SupplementalCredentials & krbtgt AES-256 / NTLM Hashes" to escalate domain privileges or crack service account credentials offline). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ IDL_DRSGetNCChanges response -> 10.10.4.22 (krbtgt attributes replicated) / ⇠#3 RESP 3) from Node ③ (#3 DC RPC Endpoint Mapper (:135)) to Node ④ (#4 CORP-DC01 (lsass DRSUAPI)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AD Naming Context (DC=corp)).
